req.title: Index shows post author name
req.statement: The system shall render the author's username alongside each post on the index page.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-032 requires that the index page (GET /) renders the author's username alongside each post. The pre-loaded fixture has one post authored by user 'test' (id=1). Tests must: (1) positively confirm 'test' username appears in the HTML response with HTTP 200; (2) negatively confirm that a non-existent username (e.g. 'ghost') does NOT appear, distinguishing correct from incorrect rendering; (3) cover the boundary where the index has exactly one post (the minimum non-empty case) and the username appears exactly once per post. Additional tests cover the case with zero posts (empty index) and multiple posts with distinct authors to ensure each author name is rendered. Assertions use exact status codes and exact byte-string matches to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_index_shows_author_username_for_existing_post
preconditions: Database is initialised with fixture data: user id=1 username='test', post id=1 authored by user id=1
actions: Send GET / to the Flask test client
expected: Response body contains b'test' (the author username)
Response body contains b'test title' (the post title)
trace: R-FLASKR-032: index page must render author username alongside each post
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_shows_author_username_for_existing_post():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data
    assert b'test' in r.data

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():

    init_db()

client = app.test_client()

    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data
    assert b'test' in r.data
    assert b'other' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_shows_correct_author_for_each_post_multiple_authors
preconditions: Database is initialised with fixture data
A second post authored by user 'other' (id=2) is inserted
actions: Insert a post authored by user id=2 ('other')
Send GET / to the Flask test client
expected: Response body contains b'test' (author of first post)
Response body contains b'other' (author of second post)
trace: R-FLASKR-032: each post must show its own author; multiple authors must each appear
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        ('other title', 'other body', 2, '2019-01-01 00:00:00')
    )
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' in r.data
    assert b'other title' in r.data
    assert b'test' in r.data
    assert b'other' in r.data

tests.name: test_index_shows_no_author_when_no_posts_exist
preconditions: Database is initialised but all posts are deleted (zero-post boundary)
actions: Delete all posts from the database
Send GET / to the Flask test client
expected: Response body does NOT contain b'test title'
Response body does NOT contain b'other title'
trace: R-FLASKR-032: boundary — zero posts means no author names rendered; page still returns 200
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.commit()
    count = db.execute('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM post').fetchone()[0]
    assert count == 0

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_shows_no_author_when_no_posts_exist():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'test title' not in r.data
    assert b'other title' not in r.data

tests.name: test_index_author_username_appears_in_html_not_just_title
preconditions: Database is initialised with fixture data: post id=1 by user 'test'
The post title also contains the word 'test', so we must distinguish author from title
actions: Insert a post with a title that does NOT contain the author name
Send GET / to the Flask test client
Check that the author username 'test' appears in the response independently of the title
expected: Response body contains b'test' (the author username)
trace: R-FLASKR-032: author username must be rendered as a distinct element, not just incidentally via title
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute('DELETE FROM post')
    db.execute(
        "INSERT INTO post (title, body, author_id, created) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
        ('uniquetitle123', 'body content', 1, '2020-06-15 12:00:00')
    )
    db.commit()

client = app.test_client()

def test_index_author_username_appears_in_html_not_just_title():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'uniquetitle123' in r.data
    assert b'test' in r.data
